description: Soy Jesús, pentester y dev full-stack. Vamos por el reto de software de monitoreo de salud para astronautas: un prototipo con IA que detecta anomalías y las muestra en un panel claro. Buscamos: análisis/visualización de datos, IA/ML, diseño UX/UI, ciencias de la vida o medicina, y redacción para el pitch. Roles claros, seguridad desde el diseño y todos los niveles bienvenidos. ¡Únete!
summary: AstroPulse is a health monitoring web app for astronauts on long-duration missions, built by team Houston, Tenemos Tacos for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Tlaxcala City. On long missions, astronauts face radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a hostile closed environment, and must spot changes in themselves, often with up to a 20-minute delay from Earth. AstroPulse answers one question in one glance: "Am I OK today — for me?" It combines live heart rate and heart-rate variability with a one-tap daily mood check-in, compares both to the astronaut's own 7-day baseline, and shows a clear GREEN / AMBER / RED status with one action to take. It works offline-first, queues check-ins and alerts until the link returns, and never shows GREEN on missing data. It is a prototype with synthetic demo data, calibrated to published NASA research, and does not diagnose or replace a flight surgeon.
details: AstroPulse gathers heart rate, heart-rate variability, SpO2, temperature, sleep and mood in one astronaut-first screen. The astronaut sees a large status, a live ECG trace, a 5-minute heart-rate chart and a 7-day trend against their personal baseline (mean ± SD). A daily check-in takes one tap for mood, energy, stress and sleep quality. Published rules R1–R5 decide the status: for example, resting heart rate more than 2 SD above the personal baseline for over 10 minutes is AMBER, and AMBER plus mood 2/5 or lower is RED, with actions such as rest, breathing, log symptoms and notify the flight surgeon (queued). The backend is a realistic offline-first pipeline: ingest and validate, append-only local store, on-device deterministic rule engine, alerts and action log, and a store-and-forward sync queue with LIVE / STALE / OFFLINE states. It is built as a static web app with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no login, and exports records as JSON/CSV. Its benefit is simple: an astronaut far from Earth can evaluate their own health and act immediately, instead of waiting for Mission Control. The same loop can help remote clinics, ships and polar stations on Earth. Creativity is the combination: heart rate plus mood, against a personal baseline, not population averages.
